recipes.name: Oyster Stew
ingredients_raw: 2 (12 ounce) containers fresh shucked oysters, undrained
1 pinch cayenne pepper, or to taste
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add celery and shallots; cook and stir until shallots are tender, 3 to 5 minutes.

Heat half-and-half in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add celery and shallot mixture, and stir continuously until just about to boil. Add oysters and their liquid, and season with cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper.
Cook, stirring continuously, until oysters curl at the ends. Turn off the heat and serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Oyster Stew
raw_recipe.description: This oyster stew is easy to make with fresh shucked oysters, celery, shallots, and cream for an elegant and comforting seafood soup ready in 30 minutes!

review.reviewBody:
APRIL 2010 UPDATE From: Buddy Sizemore
Over the years I've experimented with my original Oyster Stew recipe, so I wanted to share the following information with you folks. 
A nice addition to my recipe would be to finely minced one large potato (I like Yukon Gold best), then sauté the potato with the minced celery and shallots.
Also, after considering some of the comments that a couple of viewers mentioned concerning the "floating" celery and shallots that their husbands didn't particularly care for, I experimented using a microplane to finely grate both the shallots and celery then add them in with the butter and finely minced potato. Before I microplaned the celery I cut the stringy layer off the celery stalks. This is easy to do with a potato peeler This is only a suggestion for thoes who may not like the larger peices of celery and shallots but still want the flavors. I however enjoy the texture.

Another tip would be to allow the half & half or whipping cream (which ever you use) to come to room temperature. Also drain the liquid from the oysters then add it to the half & half at the beginning of cooking . This will cut down the time it takes to bring the mixture to a rolling simmer/boil.
 This is my family's favorite indlugence. 
 I ALWAYS USE FRESH OYSTERS!
Thank's to all who have posted reviews, I'm thrilled that the majority enjoy my recipe! And, with respect to the FEW negative reviews...well that just leaves more stew for the of us! 
Buddy Sizemore

I made this with canned oysters and a few tweaks to the recipe. I used 4 T. butter and it was delicious, though next time I'll cut back a little more on the butter (trying to lose a few pounds lol). I diced about 1/4 c. onion and cooked it in the butter til tender. Stirred in 1 T Old Bay and cooked some more. Drained the oysters and added them to the pan with the onion. I chopped the oysters up finely with a spoon as they heated in the pan. Then stirred in 1 t. parsley (this helps disguise the green stuff in the canned oysters, lol). I stirred in whole milk - didn't really measure, but about 3 c. Heated almost to boiling, then turned down, added salt and pepper to taste, and a dash of hot sauce. Stir well and spoon into bowl. Honestly, this tasted just as good or better than the oyster stew I got from a local restaurant known for their fresh seafood. It looked beautiful too.

Made the recipe per instructions Bay Seasoning & cayenne, 2 diced gold potatoes, peeled & minced celery, & bacon bits on top. Also cut the med. oyster in thirds for more oyster per bite. I used 1 cups heavy cream with 2% milk, but added additional cornstarch to thicken. The recipe was raved over by guests and I agree. Perhaps the best overall blend of ingredients for a oyster stew/ I have made. Thankyou!!

Heated the oyster juice by adding to the celery and shallots as they were cooking in the butter. Added diced yukon gold potato, Worchestershire sauce (~1/4 tsp) and about ~3/4 tsp of white pepper, along with the cayenne pepper/salt and black pepper. Agree with peeling the stringy layer off the celery. Great flavor and consistency with these additions.

I have always made oyster stew the same way: oysters, butter, milk, salt & pepper. Found this recipe and decided to try it.

It is AWESOME! I cooked the onions (didn't have scallions) and celery in the butter for about 20 minutes. Diced up a few small potatoes and cooked them in the microwave and added to the onion/celery/butter mixture. (These changes are all based on the original author's recommendations by the way). 

I used half n half vs. whole milk (which is what I used in my old recipe). All my grocer had was select oysters, which are quite big. Based on another person's review, I cut these in half. Cooked until curled (normal procedure for oyster stew). Added salt, black pepper, cayenne pepper, and some "slap your mama" cajun seasoning. 

This is EXCELLENT---more like an oyster chowder when you add the celery, onions, and potatoes---much more filling for a cold winter night! THANK YOU for this excellent recipe!

This was absolutely delicious! I did not have shallots, so used diced onions. After cooking the onions and celery, I whirled it using my immersion blender. I also used about 1/4 cup of clam juice to add flavor because I used store-bought oysters and there wasn’t much juice. Added some parsley, but will cut back just a bit on the cayenne pepper next time (today!). It’s a SUPER rainy day meal with lots of little crackers and a side salad! This is def a keeper!

Nothing like a bowl of hot oyster stew!! This recipe uses too much butter for my liking, and it was missing the secret ingredient - BACON!!! 
Cut up 4 slices of thick cut bacon. Fry to not quite crisp, remove and set aside. Add a couple tablespoons of butter to the bacon drippings, saute up your veggies, toss the bacon back into the mix and follow the rest of the recipe. Everything's better with bacon!!

Delicious! I gave 4 stars because of 3 minor changes. I put the celery and scallions (not shallots) in food processor for a finer chop. The second change was to add 1/4 cup flour to to the sautéed vegetables before adding 2% milk (no cream.) That was the 3rd change. This Oyster Stew was amazing and can't wait to prepare again!

Followed this recipe for our Xmas Eve dinner. Usually my Mom makes it, but I couldn't be with my parents this year so was looking to make my own. Per Mom's recipe I used whole milk and about a cup of heavy cream instead of the half & half. Prob with similar results as this recipe. And about a dozen fresh, wild caught blue point oysters, i pan fried the oysters for a few minutes in the veggie mix. Then boild the liquid from the oysters for a minute and added that to the milk. Turned out absolutely delicious! Tastes like Christmas 😉.

This recipe is fantastic!
I used skim milk and smart balance, and used some flour to make a roux with the shallot mixture to thicken. I didn't have any celery so I added some fresh spinach chopped small to add some color and 4 med-lg garlic cloves minced. And I added some tobasco. 
This was so good!

I did: 1 Cup Cream 3 Cup Milk 4 Tablespoons Butter 2 8oz can of Oyster, only drain 1 can Dash of Parsley 1 Tablespoon flour Directions: Put in 2 TBS butter let melt and add 1 TBS flour and stir till smooth. Add 3 cups milk & 1 cup cream, add salt, parsley, and pepper. Let is come to a boil and add 2 cans oyster, 2 TBS butter, and let it come back to a boil or till it foams up. Then let it sit for 10 min to cool and serve. By far the best I have ever had. Add some hot sauce to every spoon full and my son and I were in Heaven!

Great oyster stew! Just like my mother used to make when I was growing up in Baltimore. My whole family loved it. Simple and easy to cook. The only change I made was to cut back on the butter a bit and add the oysters directly to the pot with the shallots and celery. Sautee them until the the oysters have plumped up and the fringes are wavy and separated. Then add the half and half and heat it gently till ready to serve.

I used green onions instead of shallots and added 2 cups of chicken bone broth to cook a few baby potatoes before adding the cream and oysters. It was delicious and a bit heartier, so we could eat it as a meal. Delicious!
I love this recipe for oyster stew. It has come one of my families favorite on a cold winters day.

I made it with only one adaption: I used a Vidalia sweet onion in place of shallot. It was good for my husband but our daughter added garlic salt and I added kosher salt plus more cayenne pepper. It's a bit bland without that. Next time I make it, I will add minced garlic with the minced vegetables. I will also cut the recipe in 1/2 as normally it's just my husband and I.
I used Chicken of the Sea Oysters

Loved !!! My pops made it every Christmas!! I was born and raised in NewOrleans . So oysters wee always abundant . I did add small cubed mirliton.( coyote pear I think it's called also .?) good for texture.. and adds a little sweet squash flavor !! Thank you !
I added shrimp with the veggies before adding heavy whipping cream and oysters.
